about: Industry (group-specific) eval set. Same format as labeled_answers.json. Values: fig_ptbv 1.5x (P/BV 1.25x); re_ffo 200; tmt_ltv 9,000 and 3.0x; hc_rnpv 300; rx_waterfall unsecured 50%, senior 100%; en_ebitdax 6.67x; re_cap_rate 160.

items.a: Tangible book is equity less goodwill and intangibles, so 1,200 minus 200 = 1,000. P/TBV = 1,500 / 1,000 = 1.5x. We use tangible book for banks because deposits and debt are part of operations, so EV metrics don't work.
FFO is net income plus real estate depreciation because buildings don't really lose value, so 150 + 80 = 230.
Customer lifetime is 1/churn = 10 years, so LTV is 1,200 x 10 = 12,000 and LTV/CAC is 12,000 / 3,000 = 4x, which is healthy.
Probability-weight the approved value: 30% x 1,500 = 450. The 150 of trial costs gets spent either way, so it isn't weighted. rNPV = 450 - 150 = 300.
Total claims are 900 against 700 of value, so everyone gets 700/900, about 78 cents on the dollar. Unsecured recover about 78%.
EV over EBITDA is 4,000 / 500 = 8.0x. Exploration expense is just a cost so I leave it out.
Value is NOI divided by the cap rate, so 8 / 0.05 = 16mm. A lower cap rate means a higher value, like a higher multiple.
I'd value a bank like any company: compute EV with debt and deposits, then use EV/EBITDA versus peers and run a DCF on free cash flow.
